question: Which part of the central nervous system is damaged in multiple sclerosis (disseminated sclerosis)?
explanation: Disseminated sclerosis specifically targets and destroys the protective myelin sheath surrounding central nervous system nerve fibers. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h1)

question: What happens when plaque forms on nerve fibers?

options.D: Rapid regeneration of damaged nerve cells

explanation: Scars or plaques interrupt the normal flow of electrical signals traveling along the nerve pathways. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which cells in the central nervous system make and maintain myelin?
explanation: Oligodendrocytes are the specialized glial cells responsible for creating the myelin sheath in the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the role of astrocytes during the later stages of disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: They form scar tissue over damaged neural areas
options.B: They transport white blood cells into the brain
options.C: They actively regenerate lost myelin sheaths
options.D: They secrete nourishing hormones for neurons

explanation: Astrocytes multiply to form fibrous plaques, a process known as gliosis, which replaces the damaged neural tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which viral infection is linked as a trigger for disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Studies consistently show a strong link between past Epstein-Barr virus infection and a higher risk of developing multiple sclerosis. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h3)

question: How does geography affect the risk of developing disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Urbanization directly causes autoimmune nerve damage
options.B: Tropical climates consistently show the highest disease rates
options.C: Altitude changes alter cerebrospinal fluid pressure
options.D: Risk increases with distance away from the equator

explanation: People living further from the equator get less natural sunlight, leading to lower vitamin D levels, which are linked to higher disease risk. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the most common initial disease pattern seen in patients with disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Most patients start with the relapsing-remitting form, which features clear flare-ups followed by periods of recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient has sudden vision loss in one eye and pain when moving the eye. What condition does this point to?
explanation: Optic neuritis, an inflammation of the optic nerve, is a common early sign of disseminated sclerosis. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which imaging test is best for viewing sclerotic plaques?
explanation: An MRI provides detailed images that can easily spot damaged areas and plaques in the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which finding in a cerebrospinal fluid test helps confirm a diagnosis of disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Oligoclonal bands show abnormal antibody activity happening directly inside the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why are high-dose corticosteroids given during an acute flare-up of disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: To prevent the initial formation of genetic mutations
options.B: To permanently suppress the entire immune system
options.C: To permanently regenerate destroyed myelin sheaths
options.D: To reduce acute inflammation and shorten the attack

explanation: Corticosteroids work fast to calm down inflammation during an active flare-up, helping symptoms clear up quicker. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h6)

question: How do disease-modifying drugs affect the long-term course of disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: They replace damaged oligodendrocytes with healthy cells
options.B: They eliminate all risk of future viral infections
options.C: They completely cure the underlying autoimmune process
options.D: They decrease relapse frequency and delay disability

explanation: These medications adjust how the immune system behaves, which slows down the disease and cuts down the number of attacks. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h6)

question: A patient with disseminated sclerosis gets very tired by the afternoon. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise the patient to eliminate all physical activity entirely
options.B: Encourage high-intensity exercise right before bedtime
options.C: Schedule essential activities during morning hours when energy is higher
options.D: Administer sedatives to force the body to rest during the day

explanation: Energy conservation involves planning important daily tasks for times when the patient naturally has more energy. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is a regular bathroom schedule important for patients with bladder problems from disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: It stimulates increased production of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: It stops the immune system from attacking the kidneys
options.C: It prevents urinary retention and reduces infection risks
options.D: It permanently repairs damaged spinal cord nerves

explanation: Nerve issues can make it hard to empty the bladder completely, so scheduled bathroom breaks help prevent urine buildup and infections. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which complication is managed with regular stretching and physical therapy in advanced disseminated sclerosis?
explanation: Physical therapy uses specific stretches and movements to loosen stiff muscles and keep joints flexible. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h8)

question: What is a main goal of occupational therapy for a patient with progressive disability from disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Adapting environments to maximize daily independence
options.B: Conducting lumbar punctures to monitor fluid pressure
options.C: Performing surgical repairs on damaged nerve roots

explanation: Occupational therapists check home and work spaces and provide tools to help patients do things on their own. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h8)
